newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia, Italy discuss World War Two reparations.
newsitem.headline: Croatia, Italy discuss World War Two reparations.

text.p: Croatia has offered a share in its hotel industry to Italy as part of World War Two reparations, the state news agency HINA reported on Monday.
The terms of the $35 million restitution will be discussed by an expert Croatian-Italian commission in the Adriatic port of Split on Monday.

Italy's fascist regime occupied parts of Croatia, including the northern Adriatic Istrian peninsula, in 1941-43. When Yugoslav partisans recaptured the areas two years later they forced the ethnic Italian minority in Croatia to flee to Italy.
A treaty between former Yugoslavia and Italy more then 20 years ago to settle territorial and material disputes was never fully implemented.
After former Yugoslavia disintegrated in 1991, Croatia and Slovenia agreed to pay their share of Yugoslavia's restitution.

Croatian deputy foreign minister Hido Biscevic said half of the restitution would be paid in cash and the other half in stocks from the portfolio of Croatia's Privatisation Fund, comprising state-owned hotels and other tourist facilities.
